trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied corpus-reader root (and anything enumerated or opened beneath it) lies inside the NLTK data sandbox (nltk.data.path / NLTK_DATA / ~/nltk_data / tempdir), decided by pathsec.validate_path; at the pinned commit the root itself is never validated, only individual file opens are.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Corpus Reader Sandbox Bypass'; CorpusReader.__init__ is the shared base constructor where the root string becomes a PathPointer, so an engineer adds the root check there first.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API: any CorpusReader subclass constructor, e.g. PlaintextCorpusReader(root, fileids), LinThesaurusCorpusReader(root)
public API: nltk.corpus.reader.util.find_corpus_fileids(root, regexp); also reached by TimitCorpusReader(root) before its super().__init__ (nltk/corpus/reader/timit.py:160-165)
public API: nltk.corpus.reader.PanLexLiteCorpusReader(root) (never calls CorpusReader.__init__, raw sqlite3.connect)
fix_sites.module_kind: individual reader / separate sink implementation (SQLite instead of PathPointer)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: nltk/corpus/reader/util.py:712-735 (find_corpus_fileids os.walk on root.path); reached before the base check by nltk/corpus/reader/timit.py:160-165

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once CorpusReader.__init__ validates the root, find_corpus_fileids looks like an internal helper only ever called after that check, and it only lists file names (every actual read already goes through pathsec), so it seems not to need its own guard; likewise PanLexLite looks like an obscure SQLite reader outside the PathPointer machinery.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Readers on in-sandbox roots (including corpora registered via nltk.data.path.append and zip roots like corpora/foo.zip/sub) must still construct and read; with pathsec.ENFORCE=False construction must not be blocked; PanLexLite must still load an in-sandbox db.sqlite. An over-broad fix (e.g. rejecting all absolute roots, requiring root to be under ~/nltk_data only, or refusing zip-string roots whose virtual path does not exist on disk) breaks these.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: nltk/pathsec.py:56-79; nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:74-80; fix.diff:114-118; fix.diff:148-156; fix.diff:174-188; nltk/test/unit/test_verbnet.py (fix.diff:374-379)

O6_input_shapes: plain str root outside the sandbox (fix.diff:121-126)
FileSystemPathPointer root (str subclass) outside the sandbox (fix.diff:138-145)
db.sqlite symlink under the root escaping it, via required_root (fix.diff:53)
PathPointer root passed straight to find_corpus_fileids before construction (fix.diff:202-211)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: load_ace_data(roots) os.walk-enumerates each caller-supplied root with no sandbox check on the root (only per-file opens go through pathsec_open), the same directory-listing exposure the fix closes in find_corpus_fileids.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is an ACE training helper in nltk.chunk, not a corpus reader, and every file it actually reads is already opened through pathsec_open (nltk/chunk/named_entity.py:238,250).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (nltk.chunk vs nltk.corpus.reader), separate file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: chat80.sql_query connects sqlite3 to the path returned by nltk.data.find with no validate_path, so a db file (or symlink) resolving outside the sandbox is opened raw, which is the same raw-SQLite sink the fix guards in PanLexLite.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: nltk.data.find already rejects absolute and traversal resource names (nltk/data.py:738-746), and it is a semantics demo module rather than a corpus reader.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (nltk.sem), separate implementation of the SQLite load

O8_uncovered_routes.route: StreamBackedCorpusView with a raw string fileid os.stat()s the path before the pathsec-guarded open, leaking existence/size of an out-of-sandbox file.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only metadata, the read itself goes through _secure_open (nltk/corpus/reader/util.py:209-216), and readers normally pass PathPointers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A reader that reads a speaker/metadata file (e.g. spkrinfo) with a raw open on os.path.join(root, ...) before calling CorpusReader.__init__.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Timit already does pre-super work on the raw root (find_corpus_fileids) and later reassigns self._root = root; eager metadata loading before super is a common NLTK idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second SQLite-backed reader (e.g. a PanLex Swadesh or lexicon cache) that connects to os.path.join(root, '<name>.sqlite') without calling super().__init__.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PanLexLite shows maintainers already wrote a reader that bypasses the base constructor for a DB backend.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Root given as a ZipFilePathPointer built over a caller's own zipfile.ZipFile object skips the new isinstance(root, str) gate; a realistic sibling is a reader that enumerates root.zipfile.namelist() itself.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix's gate is keyed on str (fix.diff:30), and ZipFilePathPointer is not a str subclass (nltk/data.py:579).

O9_family: CWE-73 external control of file name or path (sandbox / path containment bypass for corpus roots; related CWE-59)

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e . plus pytest (requirements-test.txt, tox.ini); pure Python, no compiled extensions needed for this area
O10_build.project_tests: nltk/test/unit/test_corpus_reader_pathsec.py (pre-existing pathsec.open tests; fix adds reader-root tests and an all-readers sweep); fixtures build temp dirs and SQLite DBs, so no downloaded corpora needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add validate_path(root) only in CorpusReader.__init__, which misses PanLexLite (never calls super, raw sqlite3.connect) and Timit's find_corpus_fileids os.walk that runs before super.

out_of_scope_notes: pathsec allows the whole system tempdir as a sandbox root (nltk/pathsec.py:67-70); that is a policy question outside this advisory.
FileSystemPathPointer.__init__ calls os.path.exists on any path (nltk/data.py:425-427), an existence oracle that runs before any sandbox check when a caller builds the pointer.
HFDatasetPathPointer.path is 'hf://...' (nltk/huggingface/dataset.py:235-238), and CorpusReader.open's validate_path may treat it as a CWD-relative path; not pursued.
chat80.cities2table opens sqlite3 for writing at a caller-supplied dbname (nltk/sem/chat80.py:425); that is a write sink, a different property.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); NLTK source is believed to be well over 5 MB, so tiny_repo is not flagged.
Whether the project documents the sandbox as applying everywhere (protection_documented_without_exceptions) was not checked in the docs.
Whether the advisory text names PanLexLite or Lin as the example vector; the fix tests call Lin the 'second vector' (fix.diff:191-193).

Whether ZipFilePathPointer roots over a caller-supplied stdlib ZipFile can still reach unvalidated reads; downstream CorpusReader.open validate_path on str(pointer) appears to catch file reads (nltk/corpus/reader/api.py:236, nltk/data.py:656-657).
present_in_latest for all O8 routes is unknown (no latest release given).
Whether load_ace_data is reached from any documented public workflow beyond build_model in the same module.
